newsitem.title: CHINA: China issues first unfixed issue price state debt.
newsitem.headline: China issues first unfixed issue price state debt.

text.p: China will on Wednesday start selling its first-ever batch of state debt with no fixed issue price, the Shanghai Securities News said on Tuesday.
Finance Ministry officials said the two-year discount treasury note, the first issue for 1997, will be sold by underwriters at whatever prices the market will bear.
The issue of 20 billion yuan worth of debt will last until February 17, the newspaper reported.

"The release of the first batch of state debt with no fixed issue price is a significant experiment," the newspaper quoted an official as saying. "This will exert a positive influence on China's efforts to make state debt issues more market-driven."

After a public tender in Shanghai on Sunday, the ministry devised a weighted average price of 82.39 yuan for underwriters to buy the two-year T-note from the state, the Shanghai Securities News reported on Monday.
The note will be listed on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchange for public trading after the issue process is over.

China issued a record 195.2 billion yuan in state debt in 1996. It has yet to announce the total amount of state debt to be issued for 1997, but industry analysts expect the sum to be another record of around 250 billion yuan.
